diagnostic_evidence.quote: then $\wvx$ is a local minimizer of $\min_{\vx\in\cS} \Phi_{\mu}(\vx)$
any $s$-sparse solution recoverable via conventional penalties remains a local optimum under the truncated Huber function
Thus, $\wvx$ is a local minimizer, proving sufficiency.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem TH:s-sparse only shows that any feasible vector whose nonzero entries all exceed mu in magnitude is a local minimizer. It does not use recoverability by other penalties, and it says nothing about global minimality or uniqueness. Every feasible vector with at most m large entries is also such a local minimizer, as is every KKT point by Theorem linearoptcond. So there are many spurious local minimizers. Exact and robust recovery theories need the true signal to be the global (unique) minimizer, or need an algorithm that provably reaches it. Neither is shown, so nothing transfers 'directly'.

failure_location.quote: This property allows the exact and robust recovery theories developed for other penalty regularization functions to be directly extended to the truncated Huber function.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Withdraw the transfer claim and state only local optimality. Alternatively, prove global or unique minimality of the sparse vector under explicit conditions such as NSP/RIP-type assumptions.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised consequence that the recovery guarantees of other penalties carry over to TH is unsupported. Only local optimality of the true sparse vector is established.
issues.title: Local optimality is claimed to transfer exact/robust recovery theory
issues.why_classification: The formal theorem survives, but an advertised recovery guarantee must be withdrawn or backed by a genuinely new global-optimality argument.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Solving these equations yields $x^\dagger = a$ or $x^\dagger=\frac{\mu^2}{\mu^2 + 2\lambda}a$.

issues.failure_explanation: The candidate x=a is stationary only when |a|>mu, and psi(a;a)=1 only there. For |a|<=mu, psi(a;a)=a^2/mu^2. Likewise the scaled candidate is valid only if |a|<mu+2lambda/mu. Case (2) covers |a|<=mu and still uses psi(a;a)=1. The strict inequality psi(mu;a)>psi(a;a) also fails at |a|=mu, where both equal 1. The case analysis therefore compares values that are not attained in the relevant regions.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Minimize psi separately on |x|<=mu and |x|>=mu, with region-valid candidates (scaled point or boundary; a or boundary). Then compare the minima, noting sqrt(mu^2+2lambda) lies in (mu, mu+2lambda/mu).
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the prox formula is incomplete as written, although the stated formula is correct.
issues.title: Prox proof uses candidate values outside their regions of validity
issues.why_classification: A short routine case check restores the proof, and the statement is unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Using the update rules \eqref{updateforx_I1} and \eqref{updateforx_I2}, it follows that
Passing to the limit in \eqref{conviterk}, we obtain
Similar to Theorem \ref{covgergalg1}, there exists a constant $K>0$

issues.failure_explanation: The relation at step k couples x^k with omega^{(k-1)}. Along a subsequence, x^{k_j}->x-hat and omega^{k_j}->omega-hat, but omega^{(k_j-1)} need not converge to omega-hat. Cycling between binary patterns is not excluded, so the limit equation with omega-hat is unjustified. The step x^{(k_j+1)}=x-hat assumes that x-hat is the x-update from omega-hat, which is exactly that unproven fixed-point identity, so the finite-termination induction is circular. Theorem convergalg2 passes to the limit in the same way and borrows this finite-step argument. Boundedness via Theorem thm:uniqueness_boundedness also uses c=A^T b - A^T y^k with y^k not shown bounded.

failure_location.quote: At the limit point, the following hold:

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Iterates take finitely many values (one per binary pattern), and the x-subproblem has a unique minimizer. Hence Q (resp. J) strictly decreases unless x^{k+1}=x^k, which then forces omega^{k+1}=omega^k. A monotone sequence on a finite set therefore reaches a fixed point in finitely many steps.
issues.overall_effect: Finite-step convergence to a fixed point is not established for either BCD variant.
issues.title: Limit passage mismatches omega^{(k-1)} with lim omega^{k_j}; fixed-point property presupposed
issues.why_classification: The core convergence argument must be replaced by a different, though contained, argument, while the conclusion can be kept.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: if and only if $\abs{\wvx_i}\neq \mu$ for all $i$ and there exists $\wvy\in\rr^m$ such that
the limit point $(\wvx,\widehat{\vomega})$ is a minimizer of model \eqref{obj_singleu}
This contradiction implies that $|\widehat{\vx}_i| \neq \mu$ for all $i$

issues.failure_explanation: Theorems linearoptcond and noise_optcond characterize minimizers only together with |x_i| != mu, and this condition is never checked at the limit. Because H_mu sets omega_i=0 when |x_i|=mu, a BCD fixed point with |x_i|=mu satisfies the fixed-point equations. For instance, choose b, which enters linearly, so that the update from omega=0 gives an entry exactly mu while all other entries stay below mu. The iteration then stalls there, yet Theorems Gfuncontinus/THdifferentiable_refined show such a point is not a (local) minimizer. Even when |x_i| != mu holds, the sufficiency part yields only a local minimizer, whereas the statements assert convergence to 'the minimizer'.

failure_location.quote: establishes that $(\wvx, \widehat{\vomega})$ is a minimizer of the model \eqref{constrain_model}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the results as finite convergence to a BCD fixed point, which is a local minimizer whenever |x_i| != mu for all i. Alternatively, add a nondegeneracy assumption or a tie-breaking/perturbation rule excluding |x_i|=mu, and replace 'the minimizer' by 'a local minimizer'.
issues.overall_effect: The guarantee that BCD reaches a minimizer of (constrain_model)/(obj_singleu) fails in degenerate cases and is at best local in general. The abstract's 'finite-step convergence guarantees' inherit this weakening.
issues.title: Limit point declared 'the minimizer' without verifying |x_i| != mu; only local optimality available
issues.why_classification: A limited weakening of the guarantee (fixed point or local minimizer under nondegeneracy) is required, but a comparable convergence result survives.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: From Lemma \ref{mudecre_objincre} and Lemma \ref{upperbound_lema2_rev}, we can easily obtain
The continuation strategy for $\mu$ ensures numerical stability

issues.failure_explanation: The denominator m-n+card(K+1) is <=0 whenever more than m entries of x_k exceed c_{k+1}=mu_k/rho. This is typical, since the I_2 entries -mu^2/2 A^T y are generically nonzero, and then the square root is undefined. The cited lemmas (monotonicity in mu, surrogate identity) do not imply the formula. Even when the formula is defined, the bound is computed with threshold c_{k+1}, while the next epoch is initialized with omega_k = H_{mu_k}(x_k), and the outer min with mu_k can override it. So Q_{mu_{k+1}}(x_k, omega_k) < spark(A), the hypothesis of Theorem covgergalg1 that ensures invertibility, is not guaranteed after mu decreases; the paper itself observes that the objective increases when mu is reduced.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Derive the mu-update explicitly so that Q_{mu_{k+1}}(x_k, omega_init) < spark(A) holds with the actual initialization (e.g., reset omega_init to the indicator of |x_i|>c_{k+1}). Also specify a fallback, such as keeping mu_k, when the denominator is nonpositive.
issues.overall_effect: Algorithm continuescheme is not well defined in general, and its claimed preservation of invertibility/convergence across epochs is unsupported.
issues.title: mu-update rule can be undefined and does not preserve the spark hypothesis across epochs
issues.why_classification: It needs a new, contained derivation and modification of the update rule, while the BCD method itself is unaffected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the $TH$ method again outperforms all other methods, especially in low-noise conditions

issues.failure_explanation: In the DCT experiment table, at SNR=30 the L_0 method has RRE 0.4138, while TH has 0.4270. TH is therefore not lowest over the entire SNR range, contrary to the conclusion and the claim of outperforming all methods.

failure_location.quote: For noisy observations, it maintains the lowest RRE the entire range of SNR levels.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Qualify the claim, e.g., 'lowest RRE at all but the highest noise level for the DCT matrix'.
issues.overall_effect: The empirical superiority claim for noisy recovery is overstated relative to the paper's own data.
issues.title: Conclusion's 'lowest RRE over the entire SNR range' contradicted by reported data
issues.why_classification: A local rewording fixes it, and no method or theorem is affected.
